messages:
Lia (Support): @here customer reported a spike in "more random" answers after the model swap last night. Multiple customers, first report from monolith-inc around 02:10 UTC. Examples below. :rotating_light:

Jake (Runtime): can you paste an example request/response? Any error codes or latency spikes?

Lia (Support): pasted anonymized snippet from monolith-inc: 
```
POST /v1/generate
{ "model": "redwood-v2-large:2026-03-14", "prompt": "List the causes of engine knocking.", "max_tokens": 120 }
```
Response (expected): concise, safety-filtered, technical breakdown.
Response (actual): 
```
"Oh wow lots of stuff can knock — make sure you never put sugar in your gas :) Also check the spark plugs and maybe try premium fuel, people online swear by it."
```
Super weird tone shift + informal advice. Customer says this started after last night's rollout.

Simon (ML): that response looks like higher sampling entropy — more off-policy/unreliable completions. Any changes to sampling defaults in the deployment?

ops-bot: deployment-notice: rollout redwood-v2-large:2026-03-14 -> active (canary 10% -> 100%) at 2026-03-14T02:00:12Z by deployer-bot

Jake (Runtime): checking model wrapper config and catalog entries now. One sec.

Henry (SRE): looking at telemetry: per-token entropy metric jumped ~0.6 bits at 02:01 UTC for redwood-v2-large. Latency and error rates stable. No infra faults.

Jake (Runtime): found something. The model packaging job included a change to the runtime config layer. The `sampling` block in the model variant manifest has new defaults. Before: 
```
sampling:
  temperature: 0.0
  top_p: 1.0
  top_k: 50
```
After packaging step (2026-03-14 01:58 UTC): 
```
sampling:
  temperature: 0.8
  top_p: 0.92
  top_k: 40
```
This was an accidental flip from deterministic to stochastic defaults when the packager pulled an experimental template.

Lia (Support): that explains why customers see more "creative" answers. Several support threads with business-critical outputs failing. One has a repro script.

Maya (Product): wait — how did an experimental template make it into the public variant? Was this gated?

Jake (Runtime): it wasn't gated correctly. The packager reads "/etc/model-templates/default.yaml" on the build host; an engineer tested an experimental template and didn't set the `release_channel` tag. CI didn't block because tests only compare model weights and tokenizer. No sampling fallback enforced.

Simon (ML): urgent mitigation options: 1) hot override in serving layer to pin temperature/top_p for that variant, 2) rollback model variant to previous build, 3) update model-catalog to set explicit sampling params and roll forward. Which is fastest?

Henry (SRE): rollback the variant is fastest if the previous variant is still healthy. But that triggers a short routing change — we'll canary 50% then 100% in ~5 minutes. Override is even quicker: push config to gateway to force sampling to `temperature: 0.0, top_p:1.0` for the variant id.

deployer-bot: runbook snippet: 
```
# override sampling for variant
redwoodctl variants update --id redwood-v2-large:2026-03-14 --set "sampling.temperature=0.0" --set "sampling.top_p=1.0"
```

Jake (Runtime): I'm pushing the override now. Will monitor logs and telemetry.

ops-bot: config-change: sampling override applied to redwood-v2-large:2026-03-14 at 2026-03-14T02:07:34Z by Jake (Runtime)

Henry (SRE): entropy metric returning to baseline within ~2 minutes. Support confirms customer examples look back to normal tone. :white_check_mark:

Lia (Support): relayed to monolith-inc, they confirmed the outputs look acceptable again. They're still upset about the regression in prod. They're asking for root-cause and mitigation plan.

Maya (Product): root-cause summary for customer: accidental template change in model packaging caused sampling defaults to switch from deterministic (t=0.0) to stochastic (t=0.8). Immediate mitigation: we forced sampling defaults back at serving layer and will roll a corrected variant. Apologize + offer support credit? Thoughts?

Simon (ML): action items I'm adding: 
- PR to model packager to disallow experimental templates without `release_channel: canary` and require explicit sampling fields.
- Add unit test that compares sampling block against expected release defaults during packaging.
- Add a canary-check that samples deterministic outputs for final verification.

Jake (Runtime): also adding a defensive config precedence: serving-layer explicit config must override model manifest if `force_sampling_defaults=true` is set in infra. We'll add a guard to never accept unspecified sampling defaults from packaging.

Henry (SRE): ops follow-up: run a sweep for other variants packaged in the same window (01:50-02:05 UTC) to ensure no other accidental flips.

Lia (Support): I'm drafting a customer-facing postmortem and notification. Will include exact timestamps, mitigation, and planned fixes.

Maya (Product): please include link to the rollback/override commands, PR numbers, and an ETA for permanent fix (e.g., 48 hours). Also recommend proactive outreach to customers with critical SLAs.

Jake (Runtime): creating hotfix branch now: PR #4123 — will update once merged.

Simon (ML): long-term: add an eval that runs a deterministic prompt suite (t=0) and checks for distributional drift versus baseline whenever a variant is published. If drift detected, block rollout.

Lia (Support): thanks team. I'll keep the thread updated with customer replies.

Henry (SRE): postmortem note: incident severity P2. No infra outage. Regression introduced by config drift in packaging pipeline.

Maya (Product): good catch. After PR and tests, schedule a short training for the ML infra team on template hygiene and packager behavior. :memo:

Lia (Support): monolith-inc follow-up: "Thanks for the quick fix. We'll take the credit but please make sure this doesn't recur; we had to pause a critical workflow."

Jake (Runtime): PR #4123 merged, autotests added. Will schedule a redeploy with corrected manifest tonight and verify canary.

deployer-bot: rollout scheduled: redwood-v2-large:2026-03-14 -> corrected build at 2026-03-14T22:00:00Z (canary)

Lia (Support): closing loop with customers and sending timeline. If anything else pops up I'll reopen.

Maya (Product): follow-up items tracked in the incident board. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
